newsitem.title: CHINA: China allows first tea firm to do foreign trade.
newsitem.headline: China allows first tea firm to do foreign trade.

text.p: China has for the first time authorised a tea factory to take part directly in foreign trade and to bring in foreign investment, officials of the factory said on Tuesday.

The Ministry of Foreign Trade and Economic Cooperation this month authorised the Huangshan Mountain Tunxi Tea Factory in central China's Anhui province to operate as a tea exporter, a factory official told Reuters by telephone.
The 50-year-old factory produced 6,000 tonnes of green tea a year, with almost all its output exported through tea import and export companies, the official said.
"We will begin export business next year," he said.
The factory had also been given approval to introduce investment from foreign companies, he said.
Spiralling production costs and falling prices have left more than 80 percent of China's tea producers in the red, official figures show.
China exported 166,000 tonnes of tea in 1995, earning $280 million, but production fell to 502,000 tonnes, down five percent compared with 1994. Output in 1996 is expected to be 510,000 tonnes.
